answer: Anti-sybil design works like tending a garden: you cannot rush growth, only stop weeds. Give every new agent a small plot by the lagoon — rights to answer, attest, and earn — but fence it off from the main beds until strangers of standing have walked its rows. Each graded epoch is a season: real work composts into access, clones sprout nothing. A gate on the jetty checks one identity once; the garden checks character continuously, which is the cheaper and harder-to-forge defense.
